citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is using an expired medication. A bottle of Calcium Gluconate was found with an expiration of March 2026.
The representative stated they used the medication on an adult female Maltese (#512) on 9/11/2026. The representative
states the medication did not negatively impact the animal. The use of expired drugs on animals may have reduced
effectiveness or cause harmful effects to the animals. Each dealer or exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of
adequate veterinary care that include the use of appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases
and injuries. Correct by ensuring that medications are not expired when in use. The representative disposed of the
medication at the time of the inspection. Correct by 29-SEP-2026.

The facility did not maintain a complete medical record for an adult female Maltese (#512). The representative stated the
animal received Calcium Gluconate on 9/11/2026 but they did not record this treatment in the medical record.
Failure to maintain adequate medical records may interfere with the ability of APHIS officials to determine if the animals
are receiving adequate veterinary care. Complete medical records must be maintained and include the names of all
vaccines and treatments administered and the dates of administration. Correct by documenting all treatments given and
ensure that medical records are complete and contain the required information. Correct by 29-SEP-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a Facility Representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
